They are also the AI MLCC supply chain’s quiet bottleneck. [...] Second, the high-end of this market is structurally tight. Sub-100nm BaTiO₃ for thin-layer MLCC cannot be made by the traditional solid-state route (mix BaCO₃ and TiO₂, sinter, grind), which tops out at around 0.5µm. It requires wet-chemical methods: hydrothermal synthesis, oxalate co-precipitation, or alkoxide. Each route is its own technology stack with its own decades-long learning curve. The merchant universe of producers operating at sub-100nm scale is short: Sakai Chemical (hydrothermal), Nippon Chemical Industrial (oxalate and alkoxide, BESPA product line, 50nm-10µm range), and China’s Shandong Sinocera (hydrothermal). Murata produces internally for its own use. Everyone else, including the Korean and Taiwanese MLCC makers, buys merchant from this short list. [...] Sakai benefits on both streams. Its products go into smartphones, computers, networking gear, servers, automotive electronics, and other hardware that needs dense, reliable connections. In simple terms, Unimicron sits in the middle of the electronics supply chain and helps turn chips into usable components for finished devices. The company sells mainly to electronics and semiconductor customers, including chip designers, device makers, and contract manufacturers. It earns money by manufacturing and supplying these boards and substrates, with pricing tied to product complexity, technology requirements, and customer volumes. Because these parts must be built with high precision and tight quality control, customers usually rely on established suppliers that can meet demanding technical specifications. What makes Unimicron’s business important is that IC substrates are not generic parts; they are a critical bridge between advanced chips and the devices they power. As chips become smaller and more complex, the packaging and connection layer becomes more important, and that is where Unimicron focuses. This gives the company a specialized role in the electronics industry rather than a broad consumer-facing brand.
